curation.notes: Methods paper (SmartTrap): an automated counterpropagating dual-beam optical tweezers (MiniTweezers-derived, light-momentum force detection) with a micropipette in a microfluidic chamber. Demonstrated on lambda-DNA F3 fragment pulling/overstretching (trapped bead vs. pipette bead), human red blood cell stretching, and electrostatic repulsion between colloidal polystyrene particles.

evidence.snippet: In the case of the particle characterization experiments, we use the tabulated value for μ for water at room temperature (21 ∘C) and 0.9775 mPa
The sampling of the PSDs is triggered every 64 μs by a software interrupt procedure resulting in a sample rate of 15.625 kHz.
The anti-digoxigenin particles are around 3.4 μm in diameter and the streptavidin particles are around 2.2 μm, making it possible to visually distinguish the particles.

handle_sequences.annotations: Twenty cycles of PCR yielded a 490-base-pair fragment. Digestion with EagI gave back two fragments of 224 bases and 266 bases, each containing digoxigenin

evidence.snippet: The experiments presented are performed on the λ-DNA F3 fragments (11.8 kb), which has a contour length of 4.0 μm.

entities.name: lambda-DNA EagI fragment F1 (19.9 kb), minor population

evidence.snippet: Also, the F1 (19.9 kb) fragment is labeled in the preparation and approximately 10% of the attached molecules which attach during experiments are F1.
Digestion with EagI gave back two fragments of 224 bases and 266 bases, each containing digoxigenin, and each with a cut overhang (5’-GGCCG) complimentary to the cut ends of λ fragments F1 and F3.
Human red blood cells are prepared at room temperature immediately before each experiment by finger-pricking using a sterile single-use needle.

solution.notes: DNA pulling buffer. Red blood cell experiments used Dulbecco's PBS 10x diluted 25-fold in Milli-Q water plus 10 mM glucose; electrostatic experiments used 0.1 mM and 1 mM salt or water.
